# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 114 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 53 | Coptic

---

## Saying 114

Simon Peter said to them: "Let Mary leave us, for women are not worthy of life." Jesus said: "Look, I will guide her so as to make her male, so that she too may become a living spirit resembling you males. For every woman who makes herself male will enter the kingdom of heaven."

---

**Translator's Notes (EMET):**

- The final saying of the Gospel of Thomas; unique to this gospel
- **ⲥⲓⲙⲱⲛ ⲡⲉⲧⲣⲟⲥ** / Simon Peter: the only named male disciple to speak in Thomas
- "Women are not worthy of life" — Peter's challenge; life (*onkh*) is the Thomasine *zōē*, the true life
- "Make her male" — **ⲥⲁⲁⲧ ⲙⲙⲟⲥ ⲛϩⲟⲟⲩⲧ** / *saas mmos nhout*: Jesus will guide/lead her to become male
- "A living spirit" — *pneuma* that is alive; the ultimate Thomasine category
- "Resembling you males" — the males are the comparison group; the female who achieves this state resembles them
- "Every woman who makes herself male" — the active reflexive: she participates in her own transformation
- The saying reflects ancient gender symbolism: "male" = spiritual, rational, complete; "female" = material, incomplete
- Mary (Magdalene, presumably) is the figure who will achieve this transformation
- This is the most controversial saying in Thomas and in all early Christian texts; it must be rendered faithfully
